leads.summary: Charge-limit gating applies the first physical battery's limit to UPower's composite DisplayDevice
leads.consequence: On a two-pack machine with BAT0 at 100% without a limit and BAT1 at 80% with a 75-80% charge limit, both reporting FullyCharged, UPower 1.91.4 combines the packs into a 90%-full FullyCharged DisplayDevice. Quickshell 0.3.1 presents that composite, but --shell selects BAT0 and reports its 100% end threshold (or picks BAT0's first sysfs threshold). The new panel chargeHoldBand rejects end 100 and prints 'Fully charged' with a full glyph for the composite; BAT1's real hold is invisible until its data is inspected separately. The prior panel treated FullyCharged at <99% as held regardless of limit, so this mixed-pack case is a regression from the new gate. Match per-pack limits to the per-pack states or use UPower's per-device list to determine whether *any* pack is held instead of applying BAT0's limit to a composite.
leads.triage: behavioural -> Opus follow-up Q1; confirmed only in a niche precondition (UPower without printed thresholds, limit on second pack only); not published. Follow-up surfaced the broader UPower preset issue, published as N4.

leads.summary: A cloned weather widget cannot persist its newly added unit override
leads.consequence: With a cloned weather widget such as tester.weather, the bar supplies the mounted clone id to BarWidget, but injectPanel never supplies it to the nested Panel, which keeps moduleName=omarchy.weather. Clicking °C/°F changes the panel and widget's in-memory settings, but updateEntryInline targets omarchy.weather rather than the clone. The clone's scoped shell facade rejects that foreign id, so on reload the chosen unit is lost. With a replacement bar granted bar-entry capabilities and a configured built-in weather entry, the same wrong id could instead write the built-in entry; the confirmed failure does not depend on that additional configuration. Pass root.moduleName to the nested panel alongside bar/settings/hostWidget, and test with a clone id.
leads.triage: behavioural -> Opus follow-up Q2; refuted: clone routing via resolveEnabledId writes to the clone id; dropped

leads.summary: The weather notification ignores the new pinned unit
leads.consequence: On a metric-region wttr.in location, pin imperial in the panel and right-click Weather: the panel displays °F/mph while the existing right-click notification runs omarchy-weather-status, which calls wttr.in without ?u or ?m and displays °C/km/h. The reverse happens pinning metric for a US-region location. The override is written to shell.json but the companion command does not read it. The shipped post-boot weather hook sample also uses this command, so it can disagree with the panel. Reconcile both consumers with the panel's unit or pass the unit in from the widget, and cover the pinned-unit case.
leads.triage: behavioural -> Opus follow-up Q3; confirmed but pre-existing (script unchanged, setting existed on merge-base); dropped as out of follow-up scope

leads.summary: Launch-feedback ownership does not prevent closing a newer unrelated OSD
leads.consequence: After the launch message opens, a volume/brightness key or another OSD writer can replace the same singleton OSD. closeLaunchFeedback on a new toplevel or after 15 seconds still sees launchOsdOpen=true and unconditionally calls close, dismissing the newer OSD. The boolean tracks whether this caller once opened it, not whether it still owns the content. This interaction existed with the old detached close too, but the new direct-call ownership guard does not fix it. Have the OSD close conditionally on an owner token/message rather than indiscriminately. The new test only checks that a fast launch with no feedback does not call close.
leads.triage: hunter itself marks it pre-existing; dropped

The PR changes that same AppLibrary declaration to inject shellHost. git merge-file with the original merge-base leaves conflict markers instead of retaining both. This needs manual resolution preserving AppLibrary { shellHost: shell } and BrightnessKeys, otherwise the merged shell will not parse or one feature will be lost. The other changed power/weather panel files merge cleanly; the base-side video-background-test rewrite also merges cleanly and retains the braced-frame assertion.

leads.summary: The kept video-background fixture still fails on the current base tip, including after the PR's braced selector is merged

Both the untouched current base and a synthetic merge of this PR's bar script and merged test exit 1 with '/dev/fd/63: line 99: PREPARED_BACKGROUND_SNAPSHOT: unbound variable', after the updated magick selector assertion has already passed. This is a base-tip test fixture failure, not a new PR regression or evidence that the first-frame fix is wrong; initialize the missing fixture state to make the merged suite a meaningful signal.

leads.summary: Unstacked #8278 implements the same weather toggle with incompatible UI semantics and an actual merge conflict
leads.consequence: #8278 (which itself builds on #8277, but is diverged from #12115) adds a click-on-degree toggle and persisted settings, plus a pinned-state dot and IPC/keybinding. #12115's degree click cycles auto → metric → imperial; #8278's degree click pins the opposite of the displayed unit and a dot resets to auto. The three-way merge from #8278's own base produced two conflict regions in the very same Text/handler block, and its weather-test.sh conflicts too. Whichever handler is selected changes the click's semantics; simply including both handlers can trigger two updates per click. Reconcile the interaction and retain both tests and the clone-id fix when merging. Neither conflicted fixture can be run before that resolution.
leads.triage: factual; coordinator verified PR state and file list via gh; Opus self-check verified pinOppositeUnit; published as related-PR note

leads.summary: Unstacked #7254 also changes the bar loader at the same location, with a conflicting three-way merge
leads.consequence: #7254 solves cloned-bar create-time injection by a loader-local loadPluginBar() and also changes diagnostic/fallback behavior. #12115 solves the same create-time problem through shell.loadBar(). Merging their diffs from #7254's actual base leaves a conflict inside the plugin loader, not an independently runnable combined implementation. Keep exactly one loader path, URL reload and fallback on Loader.Error when resolving; do not reintroduce a late-only source: binding. The added #7254 plugin-bar-loader-test fixture has not been exercised on a resolved combination.
leads.triage: factual; #7254 already listed in prior public review; not repeated

leads.summary: The top-bar manual leaves the new weather unit control undiscoverable
leads.consequence: Weather now has a click target on the °C/°F label inside its popup, persisting a three-state unit override. The bar's click table still documents only its left/right/middle widget actions and the panel list has no weather bullet or unit control; searching manual/ and docs/ finds no weather Celsius/Fahrenheit or degree-label instructions. Add the degree-label interaction and how to return to automatic alongside the panel controls, as is done for neighbouring power/audio actions.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12115#issuecomment-5855980670) and the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12115#issuecomment-5857411050), checked at head `2e84f094`.

**Verified:** the two failing shell tests are resolved. The two new commits change only those two test files. The product code is unchanged, so the other findings from the earlier review still apply, and each is confirmed again on this head (by probe or mutation, and by unchanged source for the bar initial-properties note). The PR now also conflicts with current `quattro` in `shell/shell.qml`, and one new detail changes where the charge-limit findings apply (below).

| Earlier finding | Status at `2e84f094` |
|---|---|
| Two shell tests fail | **Resolved** |
| Power bar shows a charging glyph for a held pack until the panel is opened | Still present |
| Panel presents an unheld `pending-charge` pack as charging | Still present, and reachable more widely (next section) |
| Low-battery dismissal runs on every poll after the first episode | Still present (20 of 20 polls after an episode, on AC and on battery) |
| Lower-impact notes (bar initial properties, `omarchy-bar-text-color` limits, weather unit normalisation) | Still present; source unchanged |
| Optional test notes (weather cycle copy, audio fixtures, GIF case) | Still apply; the same mutations still pass |

**Verified, shell suite:** in this review's sandbox, `test/shell` now fails the same 8 of 245 files as the merge-base (8 of 242). None of the 8 is touched by this PR, and all 8 fail identically on the merge-base (most for sandbox reasons such as a missing omarchy-pkgs checkout). On the earlier head, `bar-test.sh` and `video-background-test.sh` were the two extra failures, and both pass now. `bar-test.sh` still fails if the `setSource(url, barInitialProperties(...))` call is removed (through its unchanged `loadBar` assertion); the rewritten assertion now checks only that `Bar.qml` declares the three properties. The `video-background-test.sh` assertion still fails if the `[0]` frame selector is dropped.

### The charge-limit band can come from UPower's preset, not the configured limit

`omarchy-battery-status` reads the band from `upower -i` first (`charge-start-threshold` / `charge-end-threshold`, lines 65-66) and only falls back to sysfs when those lines are missing (68-69). In UPower's source (1.90.6 and later; 1.90.5 used `60,80`), the shipped hwdb assigns `CHARGE_LIMIT=75,80` to batteries that expose charge-control threshold attributes. UPower stores those values as the device's threshold properties whether or not its own charge-limit feature is enabled, and `upower -i` prints them whenever they are above 0. On such hardware the script can print `75-80%` whatever the configured limit is.

This PR now uses that band to decide hold versus stall (`chargeHoldBand`, `power/Model.js:86-91`). Script and panel-model probe with a stubbed `upower` printing 75/80, a sysfs charge limit ending at 60%, and a `pending-charge` pack held at 60%:

| | Merge-base | This head |
|---|---|---|
| `omarchy-battery-status` | `Holding at 75-80%` (wrong band, still a hold) | `Not charging` |
| Power panel | Threshold | Charging (glyph, phrases, pulse, "Time to full") |

**Impact:** on hardware where UPower exposes its preset, a pack that reports `pending-charge` while correctly held by a limit below 75% is reported as "Not charging" by the script and as charging in the panel. The same preset also stops the new below-99% `FullyCharged` handling from telling a worn pack from a held one. These conclusions come from UPower source and stubbed probes. No live UPower daemon was observed, and how often the preset differs from the configured limit on real machines was not measured.

**Suggested change:** read the band from the same pack's sysfs `charge_control_start_threshold` / `charge_control_end_threshold` first, and use the `upower -i` values only as a fallback (or only when `charge-threshold-enabled` is `yes`).

**Merge conflict with current `quattro`:** `shell/shell.qml` now conflicts in one hunk. Quattro's d3fb0284 (#13427) adds `property BrightnessKeys brightnessKeys: BrightnessKeys { host: shell }` next to the `AppLibrary` line that this PR changes. Keeping the PR's `AppLibrary { shellHost: shell }` together with quattro's `BrightnessKeys` line resolves it. With that resolution, the merged `test/shell` suite fails the same 14 files as `quattro` alone. `quattro`'s own `video-background-test.sh` failure (an unset `PREPARED_BACKGROUND_SNAPSHOT` under `set -u`) is not caused by this PR.

**Related open PR:** #8278 (Celsius/Fahrenheit toggle) also edits `weather/Panel.qml`, `weather/Model.js` and `weather-test.sh`, with a different click behaviour for the degree label: it pins the opposite unit, while this PR cycles three stored values. The two need reconciling if both land.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of head `2e84f094` against the earlier head `181d7f5c`, merge-base `2fbac0c8` and current `quattro`, including a local conflict resolution merged onto `quattro`. Sandboxed runs of the full `test/shell` suite on all of them. Node probes of the power, battery and weather models. Targeted mutations and ImageMagick resource checks. UPower threshold behaviour was taken from UPower's source and a stubbed `upower`. No live Quickshell, UPower or PipeWire session, and panel states were computed from `Panel.qml`/`Model.js` formulas rather than rendered.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
